findings.conclusion: The proposed explicit fourth actorHost argument removes the only Actor dependency from Utility without moving state ownership. Utility retains copy, validation, arithmetic query and immutable effect preparation; queued-play already owns the preparation lifecycle and imports Actor.

The internal prepareEffect ABI changes only for barrageDamage/ftlDamage/xBlock. Migrate the sole live production caller in queued-play and three direct current fixture calls. Keep original first three arguments, return arity, detached copy and operation behavior. Non-arithmetic effects must remain usable without a host. flow-actions is not a Utility dispatcher.

Resolve actorHost exactly once after original attack/value validation, never before copy or original assert. Preserve state.player/target/value method argument evaluation, one real attackAmount/blockAmount call per prepared effect, result integer check, and FTL threshold validation after attack and overflow. Do not prebind arithmetic functions, use Combat aliases, save host in game state or add a registry.

Cold Utility no longer loads Actor, intentionally. In normal production queued-play retains its eager Actor import, and delayed host require returns the canonical Actor table. Replacing dynamic methods on that table remains observable. Whole-table package.loaded replacement between Utility initialization and preparation would differ from the old captured table and is not part of an unqualified equivalence claim.

A new private one-line utilityActorHost immediately before prepareQueued is appropriate and avoids moving or renaming the existing watcherActorHost. It adds one require position but no new queued-to-Actor unique pair.

Freeze m9_combat_protocol_baseline.lua body and preserve its original source hash. For new Defect historical comparison, pair its old three-argument call with the entire frozen old Utility in an independent VM; current VM uses actual new Utility and queued-play. Do not rewrite old protocol or fake a compatibility fallback in production.

Authenticate all changed complete outer owners and fresh linked owner reads, then project exact bytes into existing epoch chain. Preserve original frozen fixtures, proof hashes, assertions and archives. Source-prefix and inverse tests in defect-utility-planning need a verified old-epoch projection, while current API and full graph tests must still read actual current sources.

Watcher boundary currently requires exactly two queued-to-Actor positions. Preserve those two exact historical sites and explicitly require the third utilityActorHost site in current graph; do not weaken to an inequality or delete the historical count contract.

Existing full-graph evidence has SCC sizes 68/11/2; edge-removal counterfactual yields 67/11/2 and large-SCC positions/pairs 513/324 to 510/321. A separate Utility host adds a surviving internal queued-to-Actor position, so final measured large-SCC position total is expected 511 rather than 510. This is a prediction only; remeasure complete current graph and report all absolute values, internal edges and residual risks.
